prompt_values.plan:
# Plan

## Problem

`simplify(cos(x)**I)` crashes with `TypeError: Invalid comparison of complex I`. The failure occurs in `_TR56` in `sympy/simplify/fu.py` (the helper behind `TR5`/`TR6`, invoked during `trigsimp`/`futrig`). The function compares the power's exponent against numbers:

```python
if (rv.exp < 0) == True:
    return rv
if (rv.exp > max) == True:
    return rv
```

When `rv.exp` is non-real (e.g. `I`), ordering comparisons raise `TypeError` in `Expr.__lt__`. The exponent only needs to be an integer for any of the subsequent logic (`== 2`, `== 4`, `% 2`, `// 2`, `perfect_power`) to make sense, so there is no reason to run these comparisons for non-integer exponents.

## Root cause evidence

- Reproduced at the frozen base commit `1d3327b8e`: `simplify(cos(x)**I)` raises `TypeError: Invalid comparison of complex I`.
- `rv.exp` for `cos(x)**I` is the sympy object `I`, whose `.is_real` and `.is_integer` are both `False`. Exponent objects are always sympy `Expr` instances (e.g. `cos(x)**2` has `exp = Integer(2)`), so attribute-based guards are safe to apply to `rv.exp`.
- The same code path also has a latent secondary bug: with `pow=True`, `perfect_power(rv.exp)` raises `ValueError` for non-integer exponents (`perfect_power(I)` → `"I is not an integer"`, `perfect_power(x)` → `"x is not an integer"`). Because the `max` comparison currently throws first, this is masked; a fix that only guards the comparisons would expose it. A single integer guard placed before all exponent logic covers both.

## Proposed change

In `_TR56` (around `sympy/simplify/fu.py:504`), add an integer-exponent guard immediately after the existing `is_Pow` check and before any exponent comparison or arithmetic:

```python
if not (rv.is_Pow and rv.base.func == f):
    return rv

if not rv.exp.is_integer:
    return rv

if (rv.exp < 0) == True:
    return rv
...
```

Rationale for `is_integer` specifically:
- It returns a clean boolean for concrete exponents (`Integer`, `Float`, `I`, `Symbol`) and is `None` for undetermined symbols; `not None` is `True`, so undetermined exponents (`cos(x)**x`) are also left unchanged instead of raising.
- It is the check already used elsewhere in this module for exponent validity (`fu.py:615`, `1113`, `1149`), so it matches existing convention.
- The rest of the block already implicitly assumes an integer exponent, so gating on it is behavior-preserving for all currently supported inputs.

No change is needed to `TR5`/`TR6` signatures, `max`/`pow` semantics, or the `perfect_power` branch.

## Verification

A local prototype of the exact guarded block confirmed:
- All existing `test__TR56` cases still pass: `sin(x)**3`, `sin(x)**10`, `sin(x)**6` (pow False/True), `sin(x)**8` (pow True).
- `cos(x)**I` and `cos(x)**x` are returned unchanged (no exception).
- `cos(x)**2`, `cos(x)**4`, `cos(x)**(-2)` behave as before.

Validation after editing:
1. `simplify(cos(x)**I)` returns without raising (expected `cos(x)**I`).
2. `/opt/miniconda3/envs/testbed/bin/python -m pytest sympy/simplify/tests/test_fu.py -q`
3. `/opt/miniconda3/envs/testbed/bin/python -m pytest sympy/simplify/tests/test_simplify.py -q`

## Tests to add

In `sympy/simplify/tests/test_fu.py`, extend `test__TR56`/`test_TR6` with non-integer-exponent cases in the existing assertion style:

```python
assert T(sin(x)**I, sin, cos, h, 4, False) == sin(x)**I
assert TR6(cos(x)**I) == cos(x)**I
```

Also add a regression test in `sympy/simplify/tests/test_simplify.py` asserting `simplify(cos(x)**I)` does not raise (the originally reported call).

## Scope / uncertainty

The change is a one-line guard in `_TR56`. No other ordering comparison on `rv.exp` appears in the `TR5`/`TR6` path, so nothing else needs the same treatment for this issue. A broader normalization of all exponent comparisons in `fu.py` would be a larger, separate change beyond this regression.
